source: AAA gasprices.aaa.com national average — $3.973 on Friday June 19, 2026 (Day 112), down from $4.025 (June 17) and the first sustained dip below $4.00 since late March as crude held near three-month lows after the US-Iran 14-point peace MOU — signed June 17 at the Palace of Versailles (Trump) and Tehran (Pezeshkian) — reopened the Strait of Hormuz toll-free and CENTCOM lifted the US naval blockade June 18. Still ~$0.98/gal above the $2.99 Feb 28 baseline (~33% higher). Source variance: AAA's homepage showed $3.973 (June 19), while a Finder/AAA daily reading was ~$4.05 (June 18) and CNBC cited a sub-$4.00 print ($3.999) on June 17 — daily national averages differ by source/timestamp. Brent settled ~$79.85 (June 18) and ~$80.57 (June 19); WTI ~$76.60 (June 18). Pump relief from the June oil slide lags crude by 2-3 weeks; NPR/AP note higher gas, grocery and flight prices will likely outlast the war. Five states (Alaska, Hawaii, Nevada, Oregon, Washington) remain above $5; California is highest near $5.82; diesel ~$5.45. The wartime peak was ~$4.54-4.56/gal (May 6 print $4.536 via Fox Business; NPR June 17 and CFR's Max Boot June 19 cite $4.56), below AAA's nominal record of $5.016 (June 14, 2022). Watson Institute / Costs of War (Brown): Americans have spent ~$318 more per household on gasoline and diesel since the war began (via CBS). Moody's Analytics (NPR, June 17) estimates the war has cost US consumers and taxpayers ~$132 billion so far.
